history.dynasty: British cantonment-era, early 19th century; founded by Suriti (Surati) Appaiah, a military doli (palanquin) Bearer <redacted> 1814-1815; administered today by the Telangana Endowments Department
history.summary: Sri Ujjaini Mahakali Temple at General Bazaar, Secunderabad, is one of the twin cities' most famous Shakti temples and the centre of Secunderabad's Bonalu. In 1813 a cholera epidemic (also called a plague in some sources) struck Secunderabad killing thousands; at the same time military battalions were transferred from Secunderabad to Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. Doli Bearer <redacted> Suriti Appaiah prayed at the Mahakali Devastanam at Ujjain and vowed to install an idol of the goddess if the people were saved. On returning, he and his associates installed a wooden idol at the current General Bazaar site in July 1814 (the temple's completion is dated 1815 in most sources, including its Wikipedia entry). During the temple's expansion an idol of Manikyalamma was discovered while repairing a well and installed beside Mahakali. The wooden idol was later replaced with a stone idol - reported as 1864 in one source and 1964 in another (conflict - verify). Since then Bonalu has been celebrated annually as thanksgiving: the Secunderabad jathara falls on the second Sunday of Ashada, after Golconda (first Sunday) and before Lal Darwaja (third Sunday). CSV note: town 'Secunderabad' and state Telangana are correct; the temple lies in General Bazaar within Secunderabad, which falls in Hyderabad district.

name: Sri Ujjaini Mahakali Temple
town_description: Secunderabad is the twin city of Hyderabad, originally a British cantonment, and falls within Hyderabad district of Telangana. The temple stands in the bustling General Bazaar area of Secunderabad and is the cultural focal point of the city's Ashada Bonalu festivities.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad, about 35-40 km south (verify)
travel.road: In the General Bazaar area of Secunderabad; well connected by city buses and autos; street parking nearby, which can be difficult during Bonalu (verify)

visitor_information.best_time: July-August (Ashada) for the Bonalu jathara - very crowded; quieter on regular mornings
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 5:30 AM to 1:00 PM and evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify; one source lists 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-9:00 PM). Best visiting days: Sundays and Tuesdays
